title: Lexicographically Minimum String After Removing Stars
summary: Given a string s that may contain any number of '*', remove all '*' characters by performing the following operation as many times as necessary: 1.
statement: Given a string s that may contain any number of '*', remove all '*' characters by performing the following operation as many times as necessary: 1. Identify the leftmost '*'. 2. Remove the leftmost '*' and the smallest non-'*' character to its left. If there are multiple smallest characters, any one of them can be removed. Return the lexicographically smallest string that results after all '*' characters have been removed.
constraints: s contains lowercase letters and stars, and every star has at least one surviving letter to its left.
Process stars from left to right; each removes itself and one smallest surviving letter to its left.
When that smallest letter occurs multiple times, remove its rightmost occurrence to obtain the lexicographically smallest final string.
hints: The letter value must be smallest; among equal candidates, preserving the earlier copy makes the remaining string lexicographically smaller.
Keep one stack of indices per letter and mark the rightmost index from the first nonempty letter stack.
Scan s; push letter indices; at star scan a..z, pop one index, and mark both positions removed.
The exchange rule chooses the optimal deletion at every forced star without affecting which letter values remain eligible later.
editorial: The exchange rule chooses the optimal deletion at every forced star without affecting which letter values remain eligible later.

tests.explanation: The smallest eligible letter is a; deleting its rightmost occurrence leaves aab.
The first star removes a, then the second removes b, leaving cde.
